Welcome
Welcome to RKPS, thank you for stopping by. We are located in Woodingdean, East Brighton, surrounded by the beautiful South Downs. Our school benefits from glorious outdoor spaces including two sports fields, three playgrounds and our own magical Forest School.
I am extremely proud to be the Headteacher of our dynamic learning community. We are very much a family here and we support each other on our learning adventures.
We are an academic school-our children enjoy achieving. Our curriculum is always evolving and forever creative: pupils enjoy a variety of subjects. We are artists, coders and scientists; historians, musicians and authors.
Our sporting culture is long established and our children are provided with myriad opportunities to embrace exercise and fall in love with sport. We believe that there is a sport out there for everyone.
Outdoor learning is a key component of our curriculum. Our teachers take the learning outside at every opportunity and the children's regular Forest School sessions are among their most popular.
Our fully inclusive ethos ensures that no child is left behind. Hugo, our full time therapy dog, is amongst our most popular members of staff!
I hope that this website, and school Instagram page, provides you with a flavour of what an amazing school we are but you won't fully realise until you pay us a visit. I look forward to showing you around soon.
Euan Hanington - Headteacher

Mathematics at RKPS
At Rudyard Kipling Primary School & Nursery, our Mathematics lessons foster independence and empower children to become confident problem solvers. Following White Rose Hub Mathematics means that maths resources are designed to instill a deeper understanding of mathematical concepts using a full range of fun, inspiring classroom activities. These meticulously designed lessons, and through using high quality learning materials, ensure that every child can engage with the curriculum and reach their maximum potential. Our approach encourages students to apply their mathematical knowledge to provide reasoned explanations for their solutions. For those who grasp new concepts swiftly, we motivate them to delve deeper through challenging extensions to help deepen their understanding.
In EYFS, Year 1 and Year 2 we teach Mastering Number. These short maths sessions employ the use of specialised mathematical apparatus (rekenreks) and active, short lessons of approximately 15 minutes.
The outcomes for the children:
· To develop fluency in calculation and confidence and flexibility with number;
· To be able to clearly communicate their mathematical thinking;
· To make good progress towards their Early Learning Goals and Year Group Expectations;
· To foster a positive attitude towards maths and a willingness to ‘have a go’.
Welcome Rudyard Rockstars! Times Tables Rock Stars and NumBots is back with a bang this year and the Rudyard Rockstars team are committed to helping children learn their number facts and times tables; we hope you can get behind us too in a fun and exciting way!
Each child has a personal login which they can use in school and at home on a range of different devices for free. Just download the app, log in and enter the rock and roll world to get started.
Once set up, children enjoy the sense of achievement that comes from answering questions and earning coins, which they use to upgrade their rock avatar. Many children thrive on the competitive element, so choose to play in a multiplayer game against their classmates or even students around the world, whilst others focus on improving their rock speed and climbing the rockstar ranks, with the ultimate goal of achieving the status "Rock Hero".
Our teaching and learning is tailored and scaffolded to meet individual needs, with some learners requiring a more personalised approach, including specific learning outcomes and provision to develop foundational skills. We provide our children with resources, visuals and representations to help them meet their learning objectives.
Helping your children with maths can sometimes be tricky.
We hope the links and documents below might help.
http://www.primarygames.co.uk/ - A variety of games to help with maths
http://mathszone.co.uk/ - A variety of games to help with maths
http://www.abc.net.au/countusin/games/game3.htm - Games to help practising counting, recognising and ordering numbers up to 10
http://www.learnyourtables.co.uk/en/index2.htm - An interactive and fun way to practise those times tables!
http://www.funbrain.com/brain/MathBrain/MathBrain.html - A variety of interactive maths games to help with counting recognising numbers, addition and subtraction as well as fractions and shape!
http://static.novelgames.com/flashgames/game_e.37.swf?id=186 - A great game for learning and recalling number bonds to 10
http://www.hoodamath.com/games/skatermath.html - A game that focuses on all four operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication and division).
http://www.ictgames.com/soccer_subtraction.html - A subtraction game that gives you the chance to score a goal!

Governors
Introducing the RKPS GovernorsAt RKPS, the Governors act as critical friends to the Headteacher and senior leadership team, to provideindependent oversight of the management and operation of a school, with the aim of improving the qualityof education provided and raising standards. Governors are volunteers, and are not involved in running theschool on a day-to-day basis; this is the job of the Head Teacher and other senior staff. Governors supportthe school through:
Participating in Governing body meetings - Full governing body meetings are normally held once a term, and consider issues such as setting the school vision, mitigating financial risks, and scrutinising educational outcomes.
Undertaking school visits - these help the Governors to understand more about the school and the reality of school life. Governor visits to classrooms are not a form of inspection, but serve as monitoring function on the implementation of the school’s plans and policies.
Attending committee meetings – there are several statutory committees that must be in place, for example Personnel, Curriculum, Premises, and Finance. Most governors are members of one or two committees, whose work is reported back to the full governing body. This is so all governors are kept informed of matters and working progress.
The current RKPS Governors are:
Alex Brewer & Craig Munro
Andrew Giles, Liz Brand, Craig Munro, Simon Blackett, Alex Brewer, Prashanth Roa, Ellie Evans
Annabel Wyatt-Dunford
Introducing our governors
As a parent of two children at the school, I believe passionately in the power of education to transform lives. I am committed to helping every child reach their potential in a supportive, inclusive, and inspiring environment.
I am a Marketing Director and subject link governor for IT. I bring experience in strategic leadership, communications, and organisational planning to my role as governor, supporting the school’s long-term vision and ensuring resources are used effectively. For me, being a governor is about making a positive difference, working alongside dedicated staff, parents, and fellow governors to maintain and raise standards for the benefit of all pupils.
I'm Craig Munro and I'm Digital Product Director at ReedPop. I am co-chair of governors, a member of the resources committee, and our subject link governor for English. I bring experience with business strategy, budgeting, and planning skills with me to be an effective governor.
I’m Liz Brand and I work for a global events company, which involves lots of planning and travel all over the world. I am Vice Chair of Governors and have been involved on the RKPS Governing board for over 5 years, I am also the link governor with our PE team.The skills I bring include, organising, planning, budgets, strategy, partnership working and marketing; it is so important to engage with the local community and show off our wonderful school to new and prospective children.
I'm Andrew Giles, have lived in Woodingdean since 2012, and I'm Head of IT at a pharmaceutical company, where I have worked for over 20 years. I chair the Resources committee, and I'm link governor for Maths. I have experience in budgeting, financial planning, cost saving initiatives, and IT.
I believe in doing something positive for the next generation, helping children realise their own potential by helping create a fair, well resourced, all-inclusive pupil centred environment where pupils can learn new skills to help realise their dreams and be the best version of themselves that they can be. The opportunity to help maintain and raise educational standards through either creating policies to help promote effective ways of teaching and learning, or inputting into the strategic direction and financial planning of the school to make a real difference to how a school runs, is something that I find greatly fulfilling as I give something back to the local community.
Hi, I'm Mrs Brewer. I enjoy bringing my passion for music to this wonderful, vibrant community by leading our choirs, samba band and other music projects. Outside of school, I love film and theatre, and I act and sing in three drama groups.
The opportunity to contribute to a school's success as a governor resonates deeply with a commitment to community service and a thriving educational environment. I believe that by championing kindness and respect, we create a nurturing space where every student feels valued and empowered. Dedication to equality and inclusion ensures that all voices are heard and every child has the opportunity to flourish, regardless of their background or circumstances. A positive school culture that inspires both students and staff, alongside active promotion of teamwork, is crucial for achieving educational excellence. Furthermore, ensuring financial sustainability is vital for providing the best possible resources and a stable environment, directly enhancing the learning experience for students and supporting the work of staff. I thank you all for the opportunity to serve our school and community.
I'm delighted to have the opportunity to help shape a school that I’ve come to love so much since my daughter joined the nursery. I care deeply about RKPS and its success, and I am motivated by creating a sense of community and purpose, particularly for our children. I’ve volunteered as a befriender in Woodingdean for the past eight years and love participating in local sustainability projects to help build a better world for the next generation.Rudyard Kipling provides a nurturing, stable education that has enabled my daughter to thrive and I want to ensure that standards remain high, so every pupil has a chance to benefit from the fantastic teaching and the learning environment that's offered there.

Breakfast & After School Club
**TO BOOK YOUR SESSIONS PLEASE USE ARBOR PARENT PORTAL.
We are very proud of our extended services at Rudyard, they are very popular and we rely heavily on prompt payments to cover staffing costs and resources. Breakfast Club and After School Club is available to children in Reception - YR6.
The school governors have adopted a strict no debt and cashless policy. This means no parent can book any sessions for either club if a school debt is outstanding. A copy of the School Debt Policy is also included on this page along with a FAQS information sheet.
**If you are aware of any allergies, it is crucial that you inform the school as soon as possible.
After School Club - Online bookings only.
Breakfast Club - Online bookings only.
To pay for your session, please log in to your Parent Portal App. If you have credit on your account, your booking will be debited automatically. Please keep your account in credit. You will not be able to book unless you have enough money in your account
Cancellations must be made 24 hours in advance. This is due to staffing ratios being set daily.
If you do not have an Arbor Parent Portal account, please contact the school office.
Cash payments are not accepted.
If you require any help or support with the booking or payment procedure, please contact the school office.
Thank you for your cooperation in supporting the running of our extended services.
More information can be found here, including prices: Breakfast and After School Club Info
Chalkland Rise, Woodingdean, Brighton, BN2 6RH
Email: admin@kipling.brighton-hove.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Forest School - Rudyard Kipling Primary School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Forest School
At RKPS we are an outdoor learning school and we have an exceptional Forest School being led by Mr Wescott. Forest school is a long-term educational approach where learners regularly visit a natural woodland environment to engage in hands-on, child-led activities that foster personal, social, emotional, and intellectual growth. It promotes confidence, resilience, and a deep connection to nature through experiences with manageable risks, problem-solving, and supported risk-taking.
Each class has a block of sessions each year and enable a sustained impact across the school.
Child-Centred:Learning is driven by the needs, interests, and strengths of the individual child. Hands-On Experiences:Children learn by doing, engaging in practical activities like building shelters, crafting with natural objects, and exploring. Long-Term Engagement:Regular, sustained contact with the forest setting is crucial, allowing for observation of changes and development over time. Holistic Growth:The goal is to develop the whole child, fostering confidence, independence, self-awareness, and social skills. Supported Risk-Taking:Children are encouraged to take safe, supported risks, leading to increased confidence and resilience.
Play-Based Exploration:Children are given opportunities for self-directed, open-ended play in a natural setting. Nature-Based Activities:Activities can include building, climbing, exploring ecosystems, identifying plants and animals, and creating art from natural materials. Developing Skills:Practitioners facilitate learning, helping children develop practical bushcraft skills, communication, and creative problem-solving. Connecting to the Curriculum:Forest School can be a powerful way to bring academic subjects to life through real-world experiences.
Due to the nature of the environment and activities, it is important that children come prepared with a change of shoes, long trousers and a coast during colder months.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reading - Rudyard Kipling Primary School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Reading
Our school library sits at the heart of our school, and our class reading areas reflect the high value we place on this aspect of our children’s education. We promote reading in all areas of our curriculum and give the children the time and space to enjoy a good book both inside and outside the classroom. Our children have positive attitudes towards reading and are able to talk about what they enjoy about reading and why it is important to them as learners. Our Reading Policy will give you more information about how this is achieved through our everyday practise at school.
Through Early Years, Key Stage 1 and Year 3, children receive daily lessons, which are fun and engaging and designed to be memorable. In addition to this, children are exposed to reading books that match their level of phonics development both in terms of decoding, problem solving and common exception words.
Here at Rudyard, we know that adults have a vital role in modelling effective language and communication when story telling. In English lessons (through our Power of Reading approach), the teachers share a high quality class text with the children. Questions are asked by the adults to help develop their understanding of the book.
Children will learn about the structure of stories, poems and information texts. An awareness of writing styles and conventions is also developed through reading so that children can be aware of these and apply them to their own writing.
Children also read weekly in small groups with the teacher. After some initial teaching and discussion of the text (which is appropriate to their level of ability) they read individually, guided by the teacher in order to develop their reading skills.
There is a reading area in all classrooms and children have regular access to our school library. Hearing stories and poems is just as important as reading them and story time is a very special time for both children and teachers. Teachers model good reading skills which help to make the texts more interesting and enjoyable to the listener. We also have Relaxing Reading time, where children can choose their own book to sit back relax and read!
We have a team of fabulous reading volunteers who work with children across the school, from Reception to Year 6 to support them in their reading. They might help the youngest members of our school use their phonics to decode new words, or have conversations with our older children to develop inference and comprehension skills. We are always looking for new volunteers. Contact Ms Forsyth, via the office if you are interested.
The link between school and home reading is invaluable. Children need to practise their reading as often as possible and the benefits of reading at least 3 x a week makes a significant difference. Your child’s reading book will be changed regularly in school, but do not limit their reading to book band/phonic books only, children may complement their school reading books with books from home.
Ensure your child has their reading record with them in school everydayPlease record when you have read with your child (doesn’t need to be very long) at least 3 x a week for the chance for them to win a new book for Blast off into Reading).We absolutely love finding out what books your child has enjoyed reading at home. Thank you for your continued support.
